children: Aclara Resources is in line for up to $750 million government-debt financing from the U.S. Export-Import Bank to build its rare-earth and metals plant in Louisiana.

The nonbinding letter of interest is in support for Project Dynamo, Aclara's planned rare-earth separation, metals and alloys facility in Port of Vinton. The company said Friday that the support would provide a pathway to bring its capabilities together at an industrial scale.
For the project, Export-Import Bank, or EXIM, has indicated that the potential financing could cover up to $750 million of costs with repayment to be done over the course of 15 years.

The plant that is part of Project Dynamo is designed to refine rare earths sourced from Aclara's South American mines into high-performance magnet materials that can be used in industries from defense and electric vehicles to artificial intelligence-powered infrastructure.
The company said it expects the facility in Louisiana to be construction-ready by the end of the year.
